title: Tokens: why AI doesn't read one word at a time
learningObjective: After one watch the viewer can say that an AI splits text into tokens, turns them into numbers, and that token counts differ from word counts and vary by model and language.

segments.text: AI Maxxing, part one of ten. AI doesn't read one word at a time. You type: Remind me to recharge my Jio plan tomorrow. Eight words.
A tokenizer cuts that text into pieces called tokens.
Here, Remind splits into Rem and ind. Jio becomes J and io.
Each piece has an ID number. The model receives those IDs.
Token count and word count differ. Eight words became ten tokens.
Language matters. This tokenizer counts an English alarm request as six tokens. In Hindi: twenty three.
Other tokenizers can split the same text differently.
Check a long prompt with your model’s tokenizer first.
A token can be part of a word. Count tokens with the tokenizer your model uses.
